correctness.rationale: Toeplitz compression is an isometry on L∞, so constant-modulus membership gives norm-distance lower bound max(M-ν,ν-m)>=(M-m)/2. Uniformly approximate h by a nowhere-zero polygonal/translated complex path on the circle and replace it by radius (M+m)/2 to obtain matching upper bounds. For a(t)=exp(1-csc²(t/2)), derivatives vanish flatly at t=0 and 2π, making a(t)exp(i/t) smooth. At a zero and a peak, an exact continuous-constant-modulus minimizer requires ν=1/2; cosine of phase discrepancy would be positive for all t>0, contradicting the phase chirp and continuity at t=0. For ε>0, truncate at s=2arcsin((1+log 1/ε)^-1/2), giving V≤1/s+O(1); on [s_α,π] where a≥ε^α, any near-best phase stays in a single phase-difference interval of length 4π/3, giving V≥1/s_α-O(1). Let α↑1 to establish lim V/sqrt(log 1/ε)=1/2. The nonattainment assertion is limited to continuous-symbol subclass, not ambient all-symbol class.
residual_risks: Published Toeplitz constant-modulus characterization is a necessary external hypothesis; no claim made of nonattainment in the discontinuous-symbol class.
